title: STAT+: Lawmaker wants government watchdog to probe TrumpRx over claims about drug savings
summary: A House lawmaker asked the Government Accountability Office to review whether the TrumpRx platform has saved Americans any money.

title: STAT+: HHS moves to allow compounding of some unapproved peptides
summary: Kennedy and his MAHA movement have embraced peptides, though there's little evidence for many of the wellness compounds.

title: Lilly’s ‘triple-G’ drug tops Novo’s Ozempic in diabetes trial
summary: The highest dose of retatrutide beat Ozempic on measures of blood sugar and weight loss, but was also associated with higher side effect rates and treatment discontinuations.

title: FDA unveils guidance for ‘plug and play’ gene therapies
summary: The plan builds on recent FDA moves to speed "personalized" treatments by offering an approval framework for therapies benefiting different subsets of patients with the same disease.

title: STAT+: Senate candidate El-Sayed wants to ‘grill’ RFK Jr., calls him the ‘most incompetent HHS secretary ever’
summary: Abdul El-Sayed has made headlines for his progressive politics and stance on Israel. But some supporters consider his public health background critical.

title: STAT+: Why every health care AI company must face Epic
summary: In this edition of AI Prognosis: A new investigation into how Epic's market dominance is impacting health tech innovation and AI adoption.

summary: Missouri attorney general warned Eli Lilly to discontinue requiring hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under 340B program

title: STAT+: Lilly’s triple-G drug beats Ozempic in head-to-head study
summary: Eli Lilly announced that its investigational drug retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic in a large diabetes study.

title: Lilly shuffles business structure; Novartis writes off part of Avidity deal
summary: Lilly intends to merge its U.S. and international divisions when a top executive retires. Elsewhere, Astellas closed in on what it believes to be a “best-in-class” cancer immunotherapy prospect.

title: What has actually caused the decline in drug overdose deaths?
summary: After years of steep increases, especially amid the pandemic, U.S. overdose deaths decreased 27% in 2024, and preliminary data from 2025 show another meaningful drop.

title: STAT+: Lilly says ‘triple-G’ drug beat Novo’s Ozempic in diabetes study
summary: Data add to expectations that the drug will be one of Lilly’s greatest growth drivers.

title: Opinion: How pediatricians like me are helping families stay calm and informed about measles
summary: “It is dizzying to have a family clamoring for the MMR vaccine in one room while the room next door adamantly opposes vaccination,” writes a pediatrician.

title: Have you been impacted by Epic’s actions?
summary: STAT is looking to learn, from people with direct knowledge, how Epic's actions impact hospitals' technology choices. Share your story with us.

title: Opinion: Freezing my eggs showed me just how anti-feminist the fertility industry can be
summary: “A few years ago, I froze my eggs — and the experience was anything but empowering,” writes physician Pooja Yerramilli.

title: STAT+: As Epic’s dominance grows, its iron grip is choking innovation in health technology
summary: A STAT investigation found that Epic selectively withholds access to patient data, disadvantaging rival software developers and stymying innovation.

title: Ferring to acquire next-gen IVF startup Gameto for up to $1.4B
summary: The buyout hands Ferring rights to a technology capable of simplifying the lengthy and burdensome process of in vitro fertilization.

summary: Missouri AG told Lilly to stop forcing hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under 340B, a sign more states are pushing back against drugmakers.

title: STAT+: After two deaths in autoimmune cell therapy trial, Artiva is shutting down
summary: Recent deaths are setbacks in drug companies’ interest in applying cancer therapy strategies to autoimmune diseases.

title: STAT+: FDA offers new details on quicker approval pathway for personalized gene therapies
summary: Rare disease advocates applauded the FDA's move to speed access to treatments.

title: Court rejects Novo bid to block Lilly obesity drug ads
summary: Novo failed to prove that Lilly’s campaign — which featured claims of obesity drug superiority — meaningfully harmed the Danish company’s sales, a federal judge ruled.

title: STAT+: RFK Jr. goes for broke in Iowa
summary: Kennedy on the campaign trail for MAHA, and new rules loom for U.S. investments in Chinese biotech.

title: Artiva to quit autoimmune cell therapy work, cut staff after patient deaths
summary: The disclosure makes Artiva the third company to recently report fatal events in an autoimmune cell therapy trial, following announcements from Novartis and Bristol Myers Squibb.

title: A possible treatment for brain-eating amoebas, found in the sea
summary: Brain-eating amoebas are hard to treat and nearly always fatal. But researchers have isolated a compound that could help stop the disease.

title: Opinion: Emergency pediatric care is now in permanent crisis mode
summary: “In 2026, the unprecedented pediatric patient crowding of 2022 has become a normal Tuesday,” write Jonathan Kohler and Mary King.

title: Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal
summary: Armed with a $300 million financing and two GLP-1 and amylin-targeting medicines, Corxel is set to become the latest weight loss-focused company to join the public markets.

title: BioNTech, DualityBio say ADC had ‘modest’ benefit in breast cancer study
summary: The companies said the findings suggest the treatment has a “limited” impact in HER2-low breast cancer, an area where AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo’s Enhertu has already set a high bar.

title: ESMO ‘26: A cancer vaccine debate, Roche’s KRAS progress and Amgen’s ‘unprecedented’ data
summary: At one of the year’s premiere meetings for cancer research, melanoma vaccine data hailed by scientists sparked a share sell-off on Wall Street, while a lung drug received a standing ovation.

title: Another autoimmune CAR-T death; Treasury zeroes in on China deals
summary: A patient who received Bristol Myers’ zola-cel died 44 days later. Elsewhere, Gilead paid nearly $1.3 billion for a potential threat to J&J’s newly approved psoriasis pill.
